subproblem.title: Each increasing coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm, |c_I| ≤ |c|
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let c ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) be an n-covector (Covector (Eucl P) n), and let I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P be a strictly increasing multi-index (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P). Let c_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I = c(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), where e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Let |c| := covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S. Here S := Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} t_J, with t_J := c(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J 0), …, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J (n−1)))² if J is StrictMono and t_J := 0 otherwise. Then |c_I| ≤ |c|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (c : Covector (Eucl P) n) (I : SimonMultiIndex n P), |euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm c
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 (coordinate bound) of the parent-supplied proof, with details filled in.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Write c_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I = c(fun i => e_{I(i)}).

1. (Unfolding the norm.) By definition, covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S, where S := Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} t_J is a sum over the finite type of all maps J : Fin n → Fin P. Here t_J := (c(fun i => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J i)))² if J is StrictMono, and t_J := 0 otherwise.
2. (Nonnegativity.) Each t_J is either a square or 0, so t_J ≥ 0 for every J.
3. (The term of I.) The underlying map ⇑I : Fin n → Fin P of the order embedding I is StrictMono (OrderEmbedding.strictMono). Also EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i) = EuclideanSpace.single (I i) 1 = e_{I(i)} for every i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). Hence t_{⇑I} = (c(fun i => e_{I(i)}))² = c_I².
4. (One term is at most the sum.) A single term of a finite sum of nonnegative terms is at most the whole sum (Finset.single_le_sum, using Step 2 and ⇑I ∈ Finset.univ). Therefore c_I² = t_{⇑I} ≤ S.
5. (Square roots.) The real square root is monotone (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt), and √(x²) = |x| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs). Hence |c_I| = √(c_I²) ≤ √S = covectorEuclideanNorm c. ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S, where S = Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} t_J is a finite sum of nonnegative terms (squares or 0).
For J = ⇑I, which is StrictMono, t_J = c_I², using EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply to identify basisFun (I i) with e_{I(i)}.

audit.reason: The exact one-line proposition matches the prose and uses the specified Euclidean coefficient norm. Strict monotonicity of I identifies c_I² as one summand; all summands are nonnegative. Finset.single_le_sum, square-root monotonicity, and sqrt(c_I²) = |c_I| prove the precise inequality. The supplied proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: An n-covector on ℝ^P is determined by its increasing-basis coordinates (Simon 6.1.2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let α, β ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) be n-covectors, i.e. continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (Covector (Eucl P) n). For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Suppose α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) = β(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), i.e. euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I, for every strictly increasing multi-index I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P). Then α = β.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α β : Covector (Eucl P) n), (∀ I : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I) → α = β
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 (sorting injective tuples) and the extensionality bullet of Step 3 of the parent-supplied proof, with details filled in.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1. Let b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis be the standard basis of E; b k = e_k by EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply. By definition, euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I = γ(fun j => e_{I(j)}). Let f := α.toAlternatingMap and g := β.toAlternatingMap be the underlying alternating maps; they take the same values as α and β.

1. (Reduction to alternating maps.) A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So it suffices to prove f = g.
2. (Reduction to injective basis tuples.) By Module.Basis.ext_alternating for the basis b, it suffices to prove f(fun i => b(v i)) = g(fun i => b(v i)) for every injective v : Fin n → Fin P. Fix such an injective v.
3. (Sorting.) Let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n. By Tuple.monotone_sort, v ∘ σ is monotone. It is also injective, as a composition of the injective maps σ and v, so it is strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective). Let I := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono (v ∘ σ) ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, so I(j) = v(σ(j)) for all j ∈ Fin n. Since σ is a bijection, range I = range v. Thus I is the increasing enumeration of range v, the multi-index I_J of the parent proof's Step 2.
4. (Tuple identity.) (fun i => b(v i)) = (fun j => e_{I(j)}) ∘ σ⁻¹. Indeed, for each i ∈ Fin n, e_{I(σ⁻¹(i))} = e_{v(σ(σ⁻¹(i)))} = e_{v(i)} = b(v i).
5. (Sign rule.) Let h be an alternating map on E with arguments indexed by Fin n, u a tuple and τ a permutation of Fin n. Then h(u ∘ τ) = sign(τ) • h(u) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Apply this with u := (fun j => e_{I(j)}) and τ := σ⁻¹, and use Step 4. For γ ∈ {α, β} this gives γ(fun i => b(v i)) = sign(σ⁻¹) • γ(fun j => e_{I(j)}) = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I.
6. (Conclusion.) By hypothesis, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I. By Step 5, f(fun i => b(v i)) = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate β I = g(fun i => b(v i)). Since v was an arbitrary injective tuple, Step 2 gives f = g, and Step 1 gives α = β.
7. (Uniformity.) No case split is needed. For n = 0 the only v is the empty tuple, which is injective, and I is the empty embedding. For n > P there is no injective v : Fin n → Fin P, so the condition in Step 2 holds vacuously and α = β (both are 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to underlying alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective), then to injective basis tuples (Module.Basis.ext_alternating with the standard basis b, b k = e_k).
Sort an injective v: σ := Tuple.sort v makes v ∘ σ monotone and injective, hence strictly increasing; this defines I := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono (v ∘ σ) ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P.
Since (b ∘ v) = e_I ∘ σ⁻¹, AlternatingMap.map_perm gives γ(b ∘ v) = sign(σ⁻¹) • euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ I for γ = α and γ = β.
The coordinate hypothesis gives agreement on every injective basis tuple, hence α = β.

audit.reason: The exact one-line proposition includes the full coordinate-equality hypothesis. Sorting an injective tuple produces I = v ∘ σ; composition with σ⁻¹ and the permutation-sign rule transfer coordinate equality to every injective basis tuple. Basis extensionality and injectivity of the underlying-alternating-map projection then prove α = β. Every step is justified, including degenerate dimensions, without relying on the parent or siblings.

subproblem.title: Kronecker duality of coordinate wedges on increasing multi-indices (Simon 6.1.1–1.2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 be the k-th standard basis vector of ℝ^P = Eucl P. For a strictly increasing multi-index I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P), let dx^I := dx^{I(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(n−1)} = wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P). Then dx^I(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) = 1. Moreover dx^I(e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}) = 0 for every J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with J ≠ I. In the project's notation: euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I I = 1, and euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = 0 for all J ≠ I.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I : SimonMultiIndex n P), euclideanCovectorCoordinate (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))) I = 1 ∧ ∀ J : SimonMultiIndex n P, J ≠ I → euclideanCovectorCoordinate (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))) J = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (dx^I on increasing basis tuples), with details filled in.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 and proj_k := EuclideanSpace.proj k, so proj_k(y) = y_k for y ∈ E. By definition, euclideanCovectorCoordinate ω J = ω(fun j => e_{J(j)}) for ω ∈ Covector E n and J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. Fix I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. It is an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P, hence injective. Put dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => proj_{I(j)}).

1. (Matrix entries.) For a, b ∈ Fin P, proj_a(e_b) = (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)(a), which is 1 if a = b and 0 otherwise (PiLp.single_apply). Hence, for J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P and i, j ∈ Fin n, proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)}) is 1 if I(i) = J(j) and 0 otherwise.
2. (Determinant formula.) Let J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. By wedgeCovectors_apply_det (SimonGMT; Simon 6.1.1), euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = dx^I(fun j => e_{J(j)}) = det M_J, where M_J := Matrix.of (fun i j => proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)})). By Step 1, (M_J)_{ij} is 1 if I(i) = J(j) and 0 otherwise.
3. (Case J = I.) (M_I)_{ij} = 1 iff I(i) = I(j) iff i = j, because I is injective (OrderEmbedding.injective). So M_I is the identity matrix entrywise (Matrix.one_apply), and det M_I = 1 (Matrix.det_one). By Step 2, euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I I = 1. This is the first conjunct.
4. (Some row index is missing from J.) Let J ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with J ≠ I. We claim some i ∈ Fin n satisfies I(i) ≠ J(j) for every j ∈ Fin n. Suppose not. Then every I(i) equals some J(j), so Set.range I ⊆ Set.range J. Since I and J are injective, Set.ncard (Set.range I) = Nat.card (Fin n) = Set.ncard (Set.range J) (Set.ncard_range_of_injective). A subset of a finite set with at least as many elements equals that set (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le; Set.range J is finite), so Set.range I = Set.range J. Two order embeddings of the well-order Fin n with the same range are equal (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so I = J. This contradicts J ≠ I.
5. (Case J ≠ I.) Take i as in Step 4. By Step 1, (M_J)_{ij} = 0 for every j ∈ Fin n, so row i of M_J is zero and det M_J = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero). By Step 2, euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J = 0. Since J ≠ I was arbitrary, this is the second conjunct.
6. (Uniformity.) No case split on n or P is needed. For n = 0, M_I is the empty matrix. It equals the identity, so det M_I = 1. SimonMultiIndex 0 P has exactly one element, so the second conjunct is vacuous. For n > P, SimonMultiIndex n P is empty, so the statement is vacuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)}) is 1 if I(i) = J(j) and 0 otherwise (PiLp.single_apply), and euclideanCovectorCoordinate dx^I J is the determinant of this matrix (wedgeCovectors_apply_det).
J = I: the matrix is the identity because I is injective, so the coordinate is det 1 = 1.
J ≠ I: if range I ⊆ range J, equal cardinalities and OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT would force I = J, so some I(i) lies outside range J.
Row i of the matrix is then zero, so the coordinate is 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).

audit.reason: The exact one-line proposition matches both prose conclusions and includes all parameters. The determinant formula gives the identity matrix on I. For J ≠ I, finite equal-cardinality ranges and uniqueness of increasing enumeration force a missing row index, yielding a zero row and determinant zero. Matrix.of ensures the intended matrix operations. The proof is complete, non-circular, and covers n = 0 and n > P.
